We received a formal notice this morning from a third-party alleging that content generated by one of our integrations with Redwood’s hosted API infringes their copyrighted material. I'm attaching the notice and a representative sample of the output (claim_notice.pdf, sample_output.txt).

Can you confirm whether Acme Health should send a formal notice under our MSA/Order Form, and what evidence you need from our side to evaluate scope and trigger any indemnity obligations? Our procurement and legal teams are on standby — copying legal@acmehealth.com.

Immediate asks:
- Please confirm the correct contact and the mailing address for a formal notice under section 7 of the MSA.
- Let us know the expected timeline for Redwood to acknowledge and start triage (we have a 10-business-day window per our internal policies).
- If Redwood requires further artifacts (training data excerpts, model metadata, API request logs), tell us what you need and how to transmit securely.

We appreciate a quick acknowledgement. Acme wants to avoid production disruptions, and we may need to pause the integration if remediation is required.

Thanks,
Sally Chen
Head of Vendor Risk & Privacy
Acme Health

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.example.com>

Date: 2026-11-08T13:08:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Third-party notice re: model output — immediate next steps

Thanks — reviewed the attached notice and sample output. Quick read: the notice is narrow (specific passages plus a claim of copied structure), but it names actual content that lines up to the output in sample_output.txt.

MSA review (high-level):
- Order Form ACME-4521 references §9 (Third-Party IP Indemnity) in the base MSA. The MSA's indemnity section reads like a standard defend-and-hold-harmless for third-party infringement of IP "to the extent caused by Redwood's service." The ambiguity is whether generated output from an upstream model counts as "Redwood's service" versus customer-provided prompts or customer content.

Recommended immediate actions:
1) Ask Acme for a formal written notice delivered per the MSA notice block (preferably to legal@redwood.example.com and registered postal notice to Legal Ops address). Provide the canonical notice address — I'll draft the text below.
2) Request the following artifacts (secure upload): representative API requests (timestamps & prompt text), full model variant name + version, and any downstream processing steps Acme runs on the content. This helps us determine causation.
3) Prepare a provisional redline that narrows Redwood's indemnity to "third-party claims directly resulting from Redwood's grossly negligent modification to the underlying model or from Redwood-provided customer training data" — but hold off proposing to Acme until we have evidence. If we need to propose a compromise, suggest a short-term joint investigation SOW + cost-share for third-party settlement authority.

I've attached an initial redline (redline_proposal.docx) with two options: defend-first (ours) or reimbursement-first (customer responsibility until evidence proves otherwise). 

I'll be available for a quick 20-min sync at 3pm PT if you want to talk through the legal framing.

Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Contracts & IP
Redwood Inference
